title: Severe Coronal Mass Ejection Warning
description: Upstream solar wind observatory at L1 reports an earth-directed CME traveling at 2,200 km/s. Proton flux expected to exceed 10,000 pfu within 4 hours, posing severe risk of memory upsets and sensor degradation.

options.label: Enter Hardened Safe Mode (NASA SOP)
options.description: Stow high-gain antenna, power down scientific instruments, and orient solar arrays edge-on to incoming proton stream.
options.riskDescription: Suspends science collection for 48 hours; zero hardware damage expected.
options.outcomeMessage: Spacecraft successfully weathered CME shockwave in Safe Mode. Subsystems restored to nominal state after proton flux decayed.

options.label: Orient Heavy Bus Heat Shield Sunward
options.description: Keep flight computer active but point reinforced bus shielding toward Sun, throttling payloads to low-power background monitoring.
options.riskDescription: Moderate SEU risk to avionics; captures unique space weather science data.
options.outcomeMessage: Spacecraft gathered unprecedented in-situ coronal shock data. Two single-event upsets corrected by EDAC memory scrubber.

options.label: Maintain Full Scientific Operations
options.description: Ignore warnings and keep optical and radar payloads observing target targets without attitude adjustments.
options.riskDescription: Severe risk of latch-up, sensor pixel blinding, and battery thermal strain.
options.outcomeMessage: CME proton strike blinded star tracker CMOS sensors, forcing an emergency autonomous reboot and permanent 4% solar cell degradation.

title: Flight Computer Single Event Upset & Star Tracker Lock Loss
description: Cosmic ray ionization induced a bit-flip in the primary flight computer attitude determination memory buffer. ADCS reported temporary loss of inertial 3-axis pointing lock.

options.label: Execute Soft Warm Boot & Ephemeris Resync (NASA SOP)
options.description: Perform controlled processor warm restart, clear volatile cache, and request terrestrial ephemeris refresh via ground pass.
options.riskDescription: Brief 45-minute pointing blackout during reboot; completely cleans corrupted memory registers.
options.outcomeMessage: Warm boot nominal. Star tracker re-acquired celestial reference frame within 12 minutes.

options.label: Switch to Redundant Standby Flight Computer
options.description: Command bus arbiter to hand over primary control authority to secondary flight computer unit.
options.riskDescription: Leaves mission with zero remaining backup flight computers for remainder of lifetime.
options.outcomeMessage: Secondary flight computer online and validated. Primary unit isolated for diagnostic memory dump.

options.label: Force Gyroscope Open-Loop Attitude Hold
options.description: Bypass star tracker and maintain orientation purely using inertial measurement unit (IMU) fiber-optic gyroscopes.
options.riskDescription: Gyroscope drift (~0.05°/hour) gradually degrades payload optical alignment.
options.outcomeMessage: Gyro drift resulted in blurred science exposures until manual star catalog uplink completed 18 hours later.

title: Reaction Wheel #2 Bearing Friction Anomaly
description: Telemetry reports motor current spike and temperature rise on Reaction Wheel #2 assembly, indicating lubrication depletion or bearing cage micro-wear.

options.label: Desaturate via RCS Thrusters & Thermal Relubrication (NASA SOP)
options.description: Fire reaction control thrusters to offload stored angular momentum, then run low-RPM thermal conditioning to redistribute bearing lubricant.
options.riskDescription: Consumes 3.5 kg of propellant; extends wheel operational lifetime by years.
options.outcomeMessage: Bearing friction returned to baseline nominal levels. Lubrication profile verified nominal.

options.label: Apply Continuous Speed Bias Offset
options.description: Shift wheel baseline speed to avoid the resonant friction speed band, avoiding thruster fuel consumption.
options.riskDescription: Wheel runs hotter; elevated micro-vibration noise on optical bench.
options.outcomeMessage: Wheel speed shifted away from friction notch. Minor high-frequency jitter noted in telescope guidance.

options.label: Shut Down Wheel #2 (Degraded 3-Wheel Mode)
options.description: Power off wheel completely and operate on remaining three tetrahedral wheels.
options.riskDescription: Loss of reaction wheel redundancy; spacecraft cannot survive another wheel failure.
options.outcomeMessage: Wheel #2 isolated. Spacecraft attitude stability maintained in degraded 3-wheel configuration.

title: Orbital Debris Conjunction Alert (<150m Miss Distance)
description: Space Surveillance Network detects defunct upper stage rocket fragment on a near-collision trajectory. Probability of collision (Pc) calculated at 1.8 x 10^-3, exceeding red-line collision threshold.

options.label: Execute Prograde Collision Avoidance Burn (NASA SOP)
options.description: Perform calibrated 1.2 m/s delta-v burn 6 hours prior to conjunction to raise orbital altitude and increase miss distance to >15 km.
options.riskDescription: Consumes 2.8 kg propellant and slightly alters orbital revisit geometry.
options.outcomeMessage: Maneuver executed flawlessly. Debris passed at a verified safe distance of 18.4 kilometers.

options.label: Execute Out-of-Plane Cross-Track Burn
options.description: Perform inclination plane-change burn to clear orbital intersection point.
options.riskDescription: Higher propellant penalty (5.2 kg) due to out-of-plane orbital dynamics.
options.outcomeMessage: Cross-track maneuver shifted orbital node cleanly away from debris track.

options.label: Do Not Burn (Accept Risk)
options.description: Maintain orbit without propellant consumption, gambling on 99.8% miss probability.
options.riskDescription: Catastrophic loss of mission if fragment impacts spacecraft bus or propellant tank.
options.outcomeMessage: Debris streaked past at high velocity within 95 meters. Spacecraft survived, but near-miss triggered automatic review by flight director.

title: Deep Eclipse Battery Thermal Undervoltage Alarm
description: Longest annual eclipse season pushes battery cell temperatures down to -8°C. Internal chemical resistance increased by 30%, causing transient bus voltage dips during payload peak operations.

options.label: Pre-Warm Battery Cells Prior to Eclipse Entry (NASA SOP)
options.description: Energize survival bus heaters 30 minutes before shadow immersion using surplus solar power.
options.riskDescription: Depletes zero eclipse battery reserve; keeps cell core temperature above +5°C.
options.outcomeMessage: Pre-warming protocol maintained nominal +8°C cell temperatures throughout 36-minute darkness pass.

options.label: Shed Non-Critical Payload Loads in Eclipse
options.description: Power down high-rate transmitters and instruments during eclipse to reduce discharge rate to C/20.
options.riskDescription: Loss of nighttime Earth imaging data; guarantees zero battery stress.
options.outcomeMessage: Reduced discharge load prevented undervoltage. Instruments safely powered up at orbital sunrise.

options.label: Bypass Heaters & Maintain Full Payload Operations
options.description: Draw full peak power through cold cells without thermal management.
options.riskDescription: Risk of lithium plating, permanent capacity fade, or bus voltage trip.
options.outcomeMessage: Voltage dipped to 24.1V, triggering low-voltage payload shutdown. Battery permanently lost 6% rated capacity.

title: Primary Polar Ground Station Uplink Hardware Fault
description: Antarctic ground tracking dish experiences azimuth motor gear failure. All scheduled contact passes for the next 72 hours are cancelled, causing science buffer fill levels to climb to 92%.

options.label: Re-route via Commercial Backup Ground Network (NASA SOP)
options.description: Contract immediate emergency tracking passes with secondary commercial mid-latitude station network.
options.riskDescription: Slight cost expenditure ($0.2M); prevents onboard storage buffer overflow.
options.outcomeMessage: Commercial network acquired downlink carrier cleanly, dumping 480 GB of buffered science telemetry.

options.label: Enable High-Ratio Lossless Onboard Data Compression
options.description: Switch onboard flight computer to gzip/wavelet compression algorithm to compress stored telemetry by 2.4x.
options.riskDescription: High CPU utilization increases computer power draw by 18W.
options.outcomeMessage: Data compression preserved buffer headroom until primary polar station restored operations.

options.label: Permit Circular Buffer Overwrite
options.description: Allow newly acquired science observations to overwrite oldest un-downlinked data.
options.riskDescription: Permanent loss of approximately 3 days of scientific observations.
options.outcomeMessage: Buffer overflow resulted in 68 GB of lost land surface spectroscopy imagery.
